census.question: How has private employment changed in the counties where it is observed?
census.caveat: Private employers only. Los Alamos breaks in 2006 and 2007 and is charted from 2008; no other county breaks.

census.question: How far apart are average private earnings across county labour markets?
census.measure: average monthly private earnings at the workplace
census.caveat: County averages over different occupation and industry mixes. Not a same-worker wage premium.

census.question: Which counties send the largest share of their workers out to work?
census.measure: share of working residents employed outside the county

census.question: Which county-to-county labour relationships are largest, and which counties depend most on a labour market outside them?
census.measure: jobs by county of residence and county of workplace
census.caveat: 981 pairs. Drawing all of them is unreadable; the view ranks and filters.

census.question: Where is housing cost highest relative to local income?
census.measure: median gross rent against median household income
census.caveat: A five-year average. It cannot date a change and does not establish a bottleneck.

census.question: Which economies are still adding private debt, and from what level?
census.caveat: A ratio of a stock to a flow; the denominator moves with the cycle.

census.question: Does a larger debt stock mean a heavier debt burden?
census.measure: private credit against private debt service
census.caveat: Debt service ratios are BIS estimates from an assumed maturity and rate. No causal claim; the point is that the two do not track.

census.question: How have credit and prices moved over decades in the major economies?
census.caveat: Annual for the World Bank series; a year cannot date a turning point.

census.question: What makes each major economy's current position different from the others?
census.measure: level, direction and historical position across dimensions
census.caveat: Not composed into a score. Each cell is one dimension.

census.question: On which dimensions does China today resemble Japan in 1998, and on which does it not?
census.caveat: Both reconstructed from current-vintage data. A comparison, not a forecast.

census.question: How has the housing stock changed by county?
census.why_refused: Two overlapping five-year averages are not a time series. Their windows share three years, so a difference between them is not a change over a known period.

census.question: Where does state spending land?
census.why_refused: No published figure allocates state spending to counties. Drawing it would require inventing the allocation, which is the whole finding.

census.question: Where does water scarcity constrain production?
census.why_refused: Physical scarcity, legal allocation and economic consequence are three different things and only basin-scale physical conditions are held. A map joining them would assert a chain the evidence does not contain.

census.question: What do out-commuters earn relative to those who stay?
census.why_refused: Earnings are published by county of WORKPLACE. The quantity this question needs does not exist in any held source.

census.question: Does a higher credit stock go with lower inflation?
census.why_refused: Twelve points across economies with different monetary regimes, currencies and price histories. Any line through them would read as a relationship nothing here identifies.

census.question: Which counties are becoming more productive?
census.why_refused: County output is not held. Employment alone cannot carry a productivity claim — that is the counting error this repository has already adjudicated once.

employment.label: Los Alamos
employment.break_note: The series moves +66% in 2006 and +32% in 2007. A count of PRIVATE employers moves that way when an employer changes ownership classification, with no job created. The cause is not established here; only the comparable window is charted.

employment.sub: Nine counties carry employer-level data. The other twenty-four have none, so they are absent from this chart rather than flat on it.

earnings.caveat: County averages over different occupation and industry mixes — not a same-worker wage premium.

housing.caveat: A county high on this chart is a place where the ratio is high. It does not establish that housing constrains anything; it is where that question would start.

dependence.default_ordering: share of the sending county's working residents
dependence.why: Ranking by volume puts the largest counties on top and hides the places most dependent on a neighbour.

credit.caveat: A stock over a flow: the denominator moves with the cycle, so a falling ratio can mean rising output rather than falling debt.

analogue.title: China's credit is still rising; Japan's had already turned
analogue.sub: The price levels rhyme. The credit direction does not, and that is the dimension the comparison turns on.
analogue.caveat: Both series are current-vintage reconstructions: the World Bank and BIS revise back-series, so neither is what was observable at the time. A comparison, not a forecast.

stock_vs_service.title: Brazil carries a heavier debt-service burden than China on less than half the stock
stock_vs_service.sub: If stock determined burden these points would lie on a line. They do not.
stock_vs_service.caveat: Debt service ratios are BIS estimates built from an assumed maturity and interest rate, not observed payments. No line is fitted: nothing here identifies a relationship between the two.
